site.tagline: Morocco, with time for what matters to you.
site.hero_copy: A morning in the medina, a road through the Atlas, an evening beside the dunes. Discover Morocco with a little more time for the things you love.
site.collection_copy: Follow the coast, spend a night in the Sahara or step away from the city for the day. Find a journey that speaks to you, and we’ll help you make it your own.
site.about_title: A lovely trip begins with a conversation.
site.about_copy: Perhaps you have a route in mind. Perhaps it’s a desert evening, a beautiful riad or simply a change of scene. Tell us what draws you to Morocco, and we’ll take it from there.

sahara-marrakech-3-days.title: Three Days to the Sahara
sahara-marrakech-3-days.summary: Mountain passes, earthen kasbahs and an evening beside the dunes of Erg Chebbi. Three days from Marrakech for those who have always wanted to see the Sahara.
sahara-marrakech-3-days.fit: A short stay in Marrakech with the Sahara high on your wish list. You’ll need to be comfortable with long drives, particularly on the final day.
sahara-marrakech-3-days.story:
The road south is part of the pleasure: the folds of the High Atlas, the warm earth of Aït Ben Haddou and the tall walls of Todra Gorge. By the second evening, the landscape opens into dunes and the pace finally slows.

Spend a night near Erg Chebbi before the long road back to Marrakech. This is a full three days, with plenty of time on the road. If you can spare two more, our slower Sahara route gives you a whole day to enjoy the desert.

imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.title: Imperial Cities & Sahara Nights
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.summary: From the courtyards of Fes to the dunes of Erg Chebbi, discover Morocco’s cities and southern landscapes on a nine-day journey from Casablanca to Marrakech.
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.fit: A first visit with a love of history, architecture and changing scenery. Full days in Fes and Marrakech give you time to settle into each city.
imperial-cities-sahara-9-days.story:
Begin among the streets and monuments of Morocco’s imperial cities, where a doorway or a small workshop can be as absorbing as a famous landmark. A full day in Fes leaves time to follow those details with a local guide.

Then travel south through mountain country and the Ziz Valley for an evening in the Sahara. Kasbahs and the High Atlas lead you on to Marrakech, with another full day to explore before you leave.

slow-sahara-5-days.title: The Sahara, a Little Slower
slow-sahara-5-days.summary: Two nights near Merzouga and a whole day with the dunes. Take five days from Marrakech to enjoy the Sahara, the southern valleys and the places in between.
slow-sahara-5-days.fit: Couples, photographers and anyone who would rather linger in the desert. The extra day gives the journey more breathing room, though there are still long drives.
slow-sahara-5-days.story:
The first evening in the desert is only the beginning. With two nights near Erg Chebbi, there’s time to visit Khamlia, explore the surrounding settlements or simply watch the light move across the sand.

The journey home follows the Draa Valley, with a night near Ouarzazate before the Atlas crossing. Choose a camp, a lodge or a night in each—the right combination depends on how you like to spend your evenings.

marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.title: Marrakech to Fes, via the Sahara
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.summary: Let the journey between two great medinas take you through kasbahs, gorges and the Sahara. Four days, with two nights near Merzouga and a full day around the dunes.
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.fit: A natural choice if you’re continuing from Marrakech to Fes and want to see the Sahara along the way. The route can also be requested in reverse.
marrakech-fes-sahara-4-days.story:
Leave Marrakech across the Atlas and spend the first night in Dades. Beyond Todra Gorge, the road leads toward Merzouga and the broad sands of Erg Chebbi.

Two nights in the desert region leave a day for Khamlia, nearby settlements and quiet time at the dunes. Then follow the Ziz Valley and Middle Atlas north to Fes, arriving somewhere entirely different from where you began.

southern-morocco-7-days.title: A Week in Southern Morocco
southern-morocco-7-days.summary: Stay among kasbahs, palm groves and valley landscapes before reaching the Sahara. A week from Marrakech with two nights near the dunes and time for the road south.
southern-morocco-7-days.fit: For those drawn to landscapes, small settlements and the south’s earthen architecture. A gradual approach to the Sahara with fewer city changes.
southern-morocco-7-days.story:
An evening near Aït Ben Haddou, palms around Skoura, the changing shapes of the Dades Valley: this journey gives the approach to the Sahara its own time and attention.

Near Merzouga, two nights make space for village visits, dune walks and a quieter afternoon. The return is broken near Ouarzazate, so the final Atlas crossing has a day of its own.

coast-desert-8-days.title: From the Sahara to Essaouira
coast-desert-8-days.summary: An evening by the dunes, a road through southern Morocco and two nights beside the Atlantic. Eight days of desert and coast, beginning and ending in Marrakech.
coast-desert-8-days.fit: For travelers who want both desert and coast and enjoy a changing view from the road. Several days involve substantial driving.
coast-desert-8-days.story:
Travel through the Atlas and Todra Gorge to a Sahara overnight, then turn west through Ouarzazate and Taroudant. By Essaouira, mountain roads have given way to sea air and fishing boats.

Two nights on the coast leave a full day for the medina, ramparts and a long lunch near the port. There’s a good deal of ground to cover between these landscapes; the reward is seeing how different one part of Morocco feels from the next.

north-sahara-10-days.title: Tangier to Marrakech: Cities & Sahara
north-sahara-10-days.summary: From Tangier and Chefchaouen to Fes, the Sahara and Marrakech. Ten days following Morocco south, with time in the medinas and a full day near the dunes.
north-sahara-10-days.fit: For a north-to-south holiday that brings together Chefchaouen, Fes and the Sahara. Particularly convenient when arriving in Tangier and leaving from Marrakech.
north-sahara-10-days.story:
Begin beside the Strait in Tangier before spending a night among Chefchaouen’s blue lanes. In Fes, a day with a local guide brings you closer to the workshops, courtyards and neighborhoods within the medina.

The route then turns south through the Ziz Valley to Merzouga. A desert day, Todra Gorge and the High Atlas lead you onward to Marrakech, without doubling back to your starting point.

grand-morocco-14-days.title: Two Weeks Through Morocco
grand-morocco-14-days.summary: Blue streets in the Rif, the medina of Fes, Sahara dunes and Atlantic mornings. Two weeks connecting Morocco’s cities and landscapes, with longer stays along the way.
grand-morocco-14-days.fit: A first Morocco visit with two weeks to explore and an appetite for variety. Expect a substantial road journey, balanced by longer stays in several destinations.
grand-morocco-14-days.story:
There’s time here to see the country change: from Rabat and Chefchaouen to Fes, then through the mountains toward the Sahara. Full days in several stops let you do more than arrive, look around and leave.

After the desert and southern valleys, Marrakech brings gardens and lively souks. The journey finishes with Essaouira’s sea air before the return to Marrakech. It’s a wide-ranging first visit, with room to add a night wherever you’d like to linger.

ouzoud-waterfalls.title: A Day at Ouzoud Waterfalls
ouzoud-waterfalls.summary: Follow shaded paths through olive groves, pause above the cascades and enjoy lunch with the sound of falling water. A full day in the countryside from Marrakech, with your own driver-guide.
ouzoud-waterfalls.fit: A day outdoors for couples, families and friends who enjoy scenery and walking. The route can be adapted, though some paths are steep and uneven.
ouzoud-waterfalls.story:
The sound of the falls reaches you before the view opens. Paths weave between fig and olive trees, revealing different angles on the cascades as you make your way into the gorge.

With four to five hours in the area, there’s time for the walk, a riverside lunch and an optional boat ride near the spray. Your driver-guide stays with your group, with a walking pace that leaves room to stop and enjoy the surroundings.

ourika-valley.title: A Day in the Ourika Valley
ourika-valley.summary: Walnut trees, hillside villages and lunch beside the river. Leave Marrakech for the Ourika Valley, with a waterfall walk at Setti Fatma or a quieter afternoon by the water.
ourika-valley.fit: For a change of scene close to Marrakech. Choose the waterfall trail for a more active outing, or spend your time in the village and beside the river.
ourika-valley.story:
As the road follows the river into the Atlas foothills, Marrakech begins to feel a world away. Terraced fields and villages line the valley, and the cafés at Setti Fatma invite you to stay for lunch.

Walk up to the first waterfall if you’d like a more active day, or keep to the village and riverbank. Either way, there’s time to enjoy the scenery without hurrying from one stop to the next.

essaouira-day.title: Essaouira, a Day by the Sea
essaouira-day.summary: Blue fishing boats, sea-facing ramparts and a medina made for wandering. Spend a day on the Atlantic coast, with time for a seafood lunch and a walk along the shore.
essaouira-day.fit: For a taste of the coast during a Marrakech stay. There are roughly three hours of travel each way, with around four hours to enjoy Essaouira.
essaouira-day.story:
Essaouira feels different from the moment you arrive: cooler air, gulls over the harbor and the Atlantic just beyond the medina walls. Walk between small workshops and galleries, then follow the boats to the fishing port.

The afternoon is yours to enjoy. Find a table for lunch, browse the souks or pause for mint tea on Place Moulay Hassan. Your driver takes care of the return to Marrakech; if a single day feels too short, ask us about staying overnight.

ait-ben-haddou-day.title: Across the Atlas to Aït Ben Haddou
ait-ben-haddou-day.summary: Wind through the High Atlas to Aït Ben Haddou’s earthen towers and the kasbahs of Ouarzazate. A full day of mountain views, village lanes and Morocco’s film country.
ait-ben-haddou-day.fit: For travelers drawn to architecture, film locations and mountain scenery, with a full day free and a liking for a scenic drive.
ait-ben-haddou-day.story:
The Atlas crossing offers a changing view at every turn: hillside villages, cultivated terraces and peaks rising above the road. Beyond the pass, Aït Ben Haddou stands in warm earth against the valley.

Explore its lanes and climb toward the old granary before continuing to Ouarzazate and Taourirt Kasbah. Film lovers can add a visit to the Atlas studios. It’s a long day, but a striking introduction to the landscapes south of Marrakech.

agafay-evening.title: An Evening in Agafay
agafay-evening.summary: Watch the light soften over Agafay’s rocky hills, then settle in for an evening meal. Open skies and desert scenery, within an evening’s reach of Marrakech.
agafay-evening.fit: An easy change of scene for a free evening in Marrakech, especially if you’d like desert landscapes without a multi-day journey.
agafay-evening.story:
Beyond Marrakech, the stone desert opens into low hills and a wide horizon. Arrive with time to take in the late-afternoon light before dinner at your chosen venue.

You can keep the evening simple—a view, a meal and time together—or add a camel ride or quad outing. We’ll help you choose the setting and agree the details before you go.

imlil-atlas-day.title: Imlil & the Atlas, by Way of Agafay
imlil-atlas-day.summary: Rocky desert, lake views and a walk among mountain villages. Follow the road from Agafay through Lalla Takerkoust and the Kik Plateau to Imlil, with a camel ride and lunch along the way.
imlil-atlas-day.fit: For travelers who enjoy a varied day outdoors, with a one- to two-hour mountain walk. We’ll plan the trail and camel ride around your group’s comfort.
imlil-atlas-day.story:
See the landscapes around Marrakech change in a single day: Agafay’s stony hills, the water at Lalla Takerkoust and the terraces below the Kik Plateau. A camel ride and tea with a Berber family bring time to pause between the views.

In Imlil, leave the road for a walk with a mountain guide. Paths lead past walnut trees, hamlets and streams before lunch in a Berber home. The return follows Moulay Brahim Gorge back toward Marrakech.

chefchaouen-from-fes.title: Chefchaouen from Fes
chefchaouen-from-fes.summary: Blue-painted lanes, small squares and the Rif Mountains beyond. Travel from Fes for a day in Chefchaouen, with time to walk, stop for lunch and enjoy the views.
chefchaouen-from-fes.fit: For travelers based in Fes with a full day available. An overnight stay gives you more time in town and a gentler pace.
chefchaouen-from-fes.story:
The road from Fes leads north toward the Rif and the hillside town of Chefchaouen. Once there, narrow blue lanes and small squares invite a slower kind of exploring.

Spend the middle of the day on foot, pausing for lunch and photographs before the return. If you’d like to enjoy the town after the day visitors leave, we can discuss an overnight stay instead.

volubilis-meknes.title: Volubilis, Moulay Idriss & Meknes
volubilis-meknes.summary: Roman remains, a hillside town and an imperial city. Discover three chapters of Morocco’s history on a day out from Fes.
volubilis-meknes.fit: For travelers staying in Fes who enjoy archaeology, history and architecture. Expect walking at exposed sites and a varied day of visits.
volubilis-meknes.story:
Begin among the open-air remains of Volubilis, where walking through the site gives a sense of the city that once stood here. Nearby Moulay Idriss brings a different setting, with a short visit and time for lunch.

Continue to Meknes for the afternoon before returning to Fes. The day’s monument visits follow current access arrangements, leaving room to enjoy the places that are open.

marrakech-balloon.title: A Morning Above Marrakech
marrakech-balloon.summary: Leave before sunrise for a balloon flight over the countryside around Marrakech. A different view of Morocco, with the Atlas on the distant horizon.
marrakech-balloon.fit: For an early riser looking for a different view of the Marrakech countryside, with a morning free and flexibility if the weather changes.
marrakech-balloon.story:
An early start brings you to the launch area while the day is still beginning. After the briefing and preparations, take to the sky when conditions allow and watch the countryside spread out below.

The flight is one part of the morning, with breakfast and transfers arranged according to your chosen session. Leave the rest of the morning open so there’s no need to rush after landing.

agafay-quad.title: Quad Riding in Agafay
agafay-quad.summary: Leave the city for Agafay’s open tracks and rocky hills. Get familiar with the quad, then follow your guide through the landscape with time for scenic stops.
agafay-quad.fit: For an active break from Marrakech, whether you’re interested in driving or joining as a passenger. Eligibility and the riding setup are agreed in advance.
agafay-quad.story:
Agafay’s terrain gives this outing its character: stony tracks, low hills and long views. A briefing and practice session at the base help you settle in before the ride begins.

Follow your guide along the agreed route, pausing to take in the scenery. We’ll make the time on the trail, transfers and driver or passenger arrangements clear when planning your outing.

merzouga-camel.title: A Camel Ride Among the Dunes
merzouga-camel.summary: See Erg Chebbi from camelback as the dunes change color around you. A short outing from Merzouga, with sunrise or sunset options and time to pause along the way.
merzouga-camel.fit: For travelers already in Merzouga who would like a short dune outing. Overnight camping and transport from other cities are separate arrangements.
merzouga-camel.story:
A camel’s measured pace gives you time to look around: the shape of the dunes, the changing light and the space beyond the next ridge. Follow a short route from Merzouga before returning to your starting point.

Choose the time that suits your stay and comfort. A 4×4 alternative can be discussed if camel riding isn’t for you, and a camp night can be arranged separately.

merzouga-sandboarding.title: Sandboarding at Erg Chebbi
merzouga-sandboarding.summary: A board, a dune and another reason to spend time outside. Try sandboarding near Merzouga, with space to practice and enjoy the views between runs.
merzouga-sandboarding.fit: For travelers already in Merzouga who enjoy being active outdoors and are comfortable walking uphill through sand.
merzouga-sandboarding.story:
Add a little play to a desert stay. Start on a suitable dune, learn the basics and find your own rhythm, with time to rest between the climbs back up.

The session is planned around the heat and wind. It works well as a local activity while staying in Merzouga; transfers and overnight camp stays are separate arrangements.

agafay-buggy.title: Agafay by Buggy
agafay-buggy.summary: Take to Agafay’s rocky tracks on a guided buggy drive. Open views, a little adventure and time to get comfortable at the wheel before you begin.
agafay-buggy.fit: For an outdoor driving experience near Marrakech, including friends or couples who would like to share a buggy. Capacity and eligibility depend on the vehicle and operator.
agafay-buggy.story:
Meet at the base, learn the controls and settle into your seat before following the guide into Agafay’s open landscape. Scenic pauses give you time to look beyond the trail.

The route responds to conditions on the day. We’ll clarify who’s driving, who’s joining as a passenger and how much time you’ll spend on the trail, alongside the transfers and preparation.

atlas-paragliding.title: Above the Atlas Foothills
atlas-paragliding.summary: See the foothills from the air on a tandem flight with a pilot. A striking change of perspective near Marrakech, planned around the day’s flying conditions.
atlas-paragliding.fit: For travelers curious about tandem flying who can leave room for weather changes in their plans.
atlas-paragliding.story:
From the launch site, the landscape takes on a different scale. Meet your pilot, prepare together and take off only when the weather and site conditions are suitable.

Keep your schedule flexible for this outing. The launch location and flight time depend on conditions, and we’ll clarify the operator’s arrangements, eligibility and weather policy before booking.

marrakech-hammam.title: Time for a Hammam
marrakech-hammam.summary: A welcome pause between days of exploring Marrakech. Choose a traditional bathhouse or a spa setting and make time for Morocco’s bathing ritual.
marrakech-hammam.fit: For a quiet break during a Marrakech stay. Tell us the setting and level of privacy you’d prefer, from a traditional bathhouse to a spa.
marrakech-hammam.story:
After hours on your feet in the medina, a hammam offers a different way to spend part of the day. Warmth, water and a slower pace make the visit as much about taking time as the treatment itself.

A neighborhood bathhouse and a spa are different experiences. We’ll discuss the setting, privacy and treatments with you, so you know what to expect and can choose what feels comfortable.

marrakech-cooking.title: A Moroccan Kitchen in Marrakech
marrakech-cooking.summary: Learn a few of the flavors you’ve been enjoying, then sit down to the meal you’ve made. A hands-on cooking class, with a market visit available for selected sessions.
marrakech-cooking.fit: For curious cooks, couples and families who enjoy learning by doing. Share any allergies, dietary preferences and your preferred language when planning the class.
marrakech-cooking.story:
There’s something satisfying about learning a dish in the place it comes from. Work through a Moroccan menu with your host, ask questions as you cook and pick up ideas to bring home.

Some classes begin with a market visit; others take you straight to the kitchen. The session ends around the table, enjoying the food together. We’ll agree the menu and dietary needs before you arrive.

marrakech-dinner-show.title: Dinner & an Evening Show
marrakech-dinner-show.summary: Bring Moroccan food and an evening performance into your Marrakech stay. Choose a venue and program that suit the kind of night you have in mind.
marrakech-dinner-show.fit: For friends, families or couples who would like an organized evening out. Your choice of venue determines the atmosphere and performance style.
marrakech-dinner-show.story:
Make an evening of it, with dinner and a performance in one setting. The atmosphere, menu and style of show vary by venue, so choosing the right one is part of the planning.

We’ll help clarify the program, drinks and transport before you decide. If you’re traveling with children or prefer an earlier finish, let us know so the evening works for everyone.

essaouira-horse-riding.title: Essaouira on Horseback
essaouira-horse-riding.summary: Leave the medina for a guided ride along the coast. Meet the stable team and follow a trail chosen for your experience, with sea air and open scenery along the way.
essaouira-horse-riding.fit: For travelers staying in Essaouira who would like time in the saddle. Tell us about each rider’s experience so the stable can suggest a suitable horse and pace.
essaouira-horse-riding.story:
A ride outside Essaouira offers a different view of the coast, away from the harbor and busy streets. Begin at the stable, where the team will discuss your experience and introduce you to your horse.

The route and pace suit the riders and conditions. Beach access is not always possible, and a gallop is not part of every ride—the pleasure is in exploring the landscape on horseback.
